long_biography.plain_text:
Falling oil prices gave Wayne Laufer an opportunity to expand Bois d’Arc when other producers were retreating. During the industry downturn of the 1980s, he acquired drilling leases at prices that would previously have been unavailable. He kept buying acreage while competitors were anxious about the industry’s future, building the exploration base for the company’s subsequent growth.

Laufer brought broad practical experience to those decisions. As well as drilling, he had learned to arrange well financing and manage land and legal work, relying on specialists for geology and geophysics. The success of his first two wells helped establish the business. His earlier partnership in petroleum consulting had paired that practical outlook with expertise in reservoir modelling and fracture stimulation.
